history.dynasty: None (modern community temple; built by Bengali Hindu devotees)
history.period: 1956 (present structure; tradition claims older 17th-century roots - weakly sourced, verify)
history.summary: Dimapur Kalibari is the well-documented Kali temple of Dimapur, Nagaland, on Kalibari Road in Railway Colony (coordinates 25.9043 N, 93.7253 E per Wikipedia). The present temple was built/rebuilt in 1956 (a Hindustan Times report of 28 September 2006 marked its golden jubilee); devotees J.C. Das and M.M. Mazumder are named as the 1956 rebuilders, and one travel source claims roots in a 17th-century structure blessed by wandering tantric saints - an antiquity claim with no cited evidence, flagged as unverified. The temple serves Dimapur's Bengali Hindu community and is a two-storeyed structure in Bengali terracotta-influenced style with a curvilinear shikhara. The sandstone murti of Kali (also called Kamalasagar Kali after the nearby Kamalasagar Lake, said to have been dug by King Dhanya Manikya in the 15th century - legend, verify) was installed during a special Kali Puja in 1956 with Vedic rites per bharattemples.com. Durga Puja and Kali Puja are the main festivals.

name: Dimapur Kalibari
town_description: Dimapur is the largest city and commercial hub of Nagaland, on the plains bordering Assam. It holds the Kachari Ruins (Dimasa kingdom), the Dimapur Kalibari in Railway Colony, the ISKCON temple at Signal Bosti, and the Swayambhu Shiva temple at Singrijan; Dimapur Airport and the railway station connect it to Guwahati, Kolkata and Delhi.

travel.road: The temple is on Kalibari Road, Railway Colony, near the railway station in Dimapur city; local taxis and autos serve the area (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; Durga Puja (September-October) and Kali Puja (October-November) are the most vibrant periods (verify).
